verdict: Trustworthy and close to ready to hand to the team. Every sampled Verevon-side claim matches verification.verevon (exactGap, constraints, approachAdjustment), and all ~45 code citations I opened in C:/dev/CoresSystem support the sentences that cite them. Examples: the session:{id} grant at browser.rs:1235, the in-memory grant Store at grant.go:61-71, the fall-through Ok(None) at agent_routes.rs:280, the org-less search cache key at search.rs:209-226, the debug URL log under ZDR at change_routes.rs:632-637, the env-gated LlmPlanner, the change_monitor-only workflowFor, ModelPlaneInvokeRequest with no schema or zdr, screenshot/pdf None in pipeline.rs, the org-less Webhook struct and the scrape UsageEvent carrying final_url under ZDR. All 22 Priority cards with a 'partial' reference verdict have taken in their reference corrections and use the corrected prevalence. None still states a refuted mechanism, such as a Firecrawl reaper, a Codex evaluate approval gate, an LRU registry, a Firecrawl browser pool, a Firecrawl allowlist guardrail or Firecrawl profile encryption. The numbers I spot-checked (40k snapshot cap, 25 steps, 2000 chars per pattern, 8 s robots timeout, 5-minute cron minimum, Apify 10 s minimum, 4 credits per format, MAX_ACTIONS 50, 7680x4320, Aside 32 ms/5 s waitForReady, 1440x900 viewport, Apify 11 webhook retries) all trace to SRC/DOC records. The six demoted items appear only in the Nice-to-have section, each with its demotion reason. No blockers. The issues are a cross-card contradiction about where OpenAPI generation lives (F-t2-005 vs F-t2-064/075), a 'how to build' that drops a verified approach detail (F-t2-009 [Content_Types].xml), a few overstatements or mis-attributions ('every reference', 'both browser references', 'one-file'), one mixed provenance tag, one 'demoted' label on an item whose tier did not change, and small duplication and sequencing tensions. All are fixable with the exact patches below.
